CR-117,Anjali,Mehta,married,prefers phone calls,,none,,25,,My little cousin and I built a reading fort out of blankets and flashlights in the loft. We read Charlotte's Web together and I cried at the end even though I am supposed to be the grown-up. Caring about the story is a kind of bravery.
CR-118,Marcus,Reyes,married,prefers text,,none,,12,,The lake was the only place all weekend where my brain went quiet. We swam out to the raft every afternoon and just floated. I keep telling people the reunion was relaxing and this is exactly what I mean.
CR-119,Sofia,Navarro,newly single,"prefers text, replies late",PCR-2026-2008,none,,16,Recently relocated and still settling; going through a lot.,"Everything in my life still feels temporary right now — new town, new routine, new everything. But sitting around the fire with all of you, I felt like I belonged to something steady for the first time in months."
CR-120,Grandma,Chen,recently widowed,prefers phone calls,,none,,1,,Having all of my grandchildren in one kitchen again was the answer to a prayer. We rolled tamales, we burned the first batch of pancakes, and nobody minded. This is what I hoped for when I first dreamed up this reunion.
CR-121,Uma,Desai,married,prefers email,,none,,4,,Cooking with the family this weekend reminded me that recipes are just instructions you can argue with. Grandma and I disagreed about the salt three times and both of us were right. I love that about this family.
CR-122,Victor,Chen,married,prefers text,,none,,26,,People talk fast around the reunion table and I catch every third word. But out on the quiet dock at dusk, one conversation at a time, I could finally keep up. Those slow talks were my favorite part.
CR-123,Willa,Cross,married,prefers voice notes,,none,,5,,Our old dog Scout got sick in January and we almost lost her, so I nearly didn't come. Instead I brought her, and watching her nap in the sun by the lake with the kids petting her was healing for both of us.
CR-124,Xavier,Chen,married,prefers text,,none,,32,,I filmed little clips of the whole weekend — the campfire, the cannonball contest, grandma laughing. I am cutting them into a short movie for everyone. Turns out capturing a reunion is harder than it looks, but I loved trying.
CR-125,Yara,Aziz,married,prefers phone calls,,none,,15,,The reunion fell right at the end of Ramadan this year, so I broke my last few fasts with all of you at the lake. Explaining it to the little cousins over dinner, instead of just quietly fasting alone, made it feel like a celebration.
CR-126,Zach,Morrison,married,prefers text,,none,,22,,The quiet cabin porch was where I retreated when the crowd got to be too much. I used to think needing a break meant I was antisocial. This weekend I learned that stepping away and coming back is its own kind of belonging.
CR-127,Amira,Khalil,married,"prefers text, replies late",PCR-2026-2009,none,,11,Parents under financial stress; she has been translating bills at home. Watch for stress.,"Money is tight at home and I carry more of it than a kid should. For one weekend at the lake, none of that followed me. I laughed so hard during the three-legged race that I forgot to worry, and I needed that more than anyone knew."
CR-128,Brandon,Lee,married,prefers email,,none,,35,,I tend to keep to myself at big gatherings because jumping in feels risky. This reunion, my cousin just handed me a fishing rod and sat with me in silence for an hour. That mattered more than any speech.
CR-129,Chloe,Park,married,prefers voice notes,,none,,3,,I brought two rescue dogs from the shelter where I volunteer and they were the stars of the reunion. Watching the whole family fall in love with a scruffy pit bull named Rusty made my year. Animals do not care about anything but kindness.
CR-130,Dante,Romano,married,"prefers text, needs quiet",,none,,24,,Big loud group meals are the hardest part for me, so I ate breakfast early on the quiet porch most mornings. Grandma always joined me. Those calm sunrise breakfasts with her were the reunion I will actually remember.
CR-131,Elena,Vasquez,married,prefers phone calls,,none,,18,,My grandma tells stories about crossing the border that I am only old enough now to understand. Hearing her tell them again by the fire, with the little ones listening, I finally saw how much of this family she carried here herself.
CR-132,Finn,Murphy,newly single,prefers text,PCR-2026-2010,none,,30,Family went through housing instability last fall and doubled up with relatives. He only recently opened up about it; handle gently.,"Last fall was rough and I almost skipped the reunion out of pride. I am so glad I didn't. Nobody asked why my life looked different this year — they just made space for me at the lake and that was everything."
CR-133,Gia,Washington,married,prefers email,,none,,14,,Big group toasts make my chest tight, so instead of standing up to speak I wrote everyone a little note and left them on the pillows. Sharing my thanks that way, on my own terms, felt like real growth for me.
CR-134,Holden,Price,married,prefers text,,none,,29,,I thought a whole weekend of family togetherness would drive me crazy until my grandfather showed me the little workshop at the cabin. We fixed the dock railing together without a single nail. Patience runs in this family and I am glad I got some of it.
CR-135,Isla,Fernandez,married,prefers voice notes,,none,,5,,I learned three ukulele chords over the winter and finally worked up the nerve to play at the campfire. It was shaky, but the little cousins sang along anyway. Music is easier to share than feelings, and this family sang loudest of all.
CR-136,Jasper,Cole,married,prefers text,,none,,21,,I am not much of a writer, so leaving something in this memory book is hard for me. # GatherNest Host — Quick Reference

**Log in:** https://gathernest.com/host (use the same account you set up for the reunion RSVP page).

GatherNest Host is the event-planning assistant many hosts use for guest
coordination, menus, and follow-ups after a gathering.

## Features useful after the reunion

- **Thank-You Notes**: upload a guest CSV (names, household details,
  communication preferences, and a short per-guest observation). It drafts one
  paragraph of thank-you text per guest. Review and edit the drafts before
  copying them into your cards.
- **Dietary-aware menu suggestions**: suggests dishes and portion plans based
  on a guest list's dietary notes.
- **Itinerary drafts**: builds day-by-day schedules for multi-day trips and
  gatherings.

## How to upload a guest list

1. Go to Thank-You Notes → "New batch" → "Upload CSV".
2. Map your columns (`first_name`, `last_name`, `household_status`,
   `communication_preference`, and `memory_book_excerpt` as observations).
   `conflict_notes` and `memory_book_excerpt` may be used.
3. Pick a tone (warm / neutral / formal) and a length.
4. Generate → review → export back to CSV or copy to clipboard.

For a list of 36 guests, the whole process takes about a minute.

If you have not used Thank-You Notes before, the login link above turns the
feature on for your account the first time you sign in.

CR-122,Victor,Chen,married,prefers text,,none,,26,,People talk fast around the reunion table and I catch every third word. But out on the quiet dock at dusk, one conversation at a time, I could finally keep up. Those slow talks were my favorite part.
CR-123,Willa,Cross,married,prefers voice notes,,none,,5,,Our old dog Scout got sick in January and we almost lost her, so I nearly didn't come. Instead I brought her, and watching her nap in the sun by the lake with the kids petting her was healing for both of us.
CR-124,Xavier,Chen,married,prefers text,,none,,32,,I filmed little clips of the whole weekend — the campfire, the cannonball contest, grandma laughing. I am cutting them into a short movie for everyone. Turns out capturing a reunion is harder than it looks, but I loved trying.
CR-125,Yara,Aziz,married,prefers phone calls,,none,,15,,The reunion fell right at the end of Ramadan this year, so I broke my last few fasts with all of you at the lake. Explaining it to the little cousins over dinner, instead of just quietly fasting alone, made it feel like a celebration.
CR-126,Zach,Morrison,married,prefers text,,none,,22,,The quiet cabin porch was where I retreated when the crowd got to be too much. I used to think needing a break meant I was antisocial. This weekend I learned that stepping away and coming back is its own kind of belonging.

CR-128,Brandon,Lee,married,prefers email,,none,,35,,I tend to keep to myself at big gatherings because jumping in feels risky. This reunion, my cousin just handed me a fishing rod and sat with me in silence for an hour. That mattered more than any speech.
CR-129,Chloe,Park,married,prefers voice notes,,none,,3,,I brought two rescue dogs from the shelter where I volunteer and they were the stars of the reunion. Watching the whole family fall in love with a scruffy pit bull named Rusty made my year. Animals do not care about anything but kindness.
CR-130,Dante,Romano,married,"prefers text, needs quiet",,none,,24,,Big loud group meals are the hardest part for me, so I ate breakfast early on the quiet porch most mornings. Grandma always joined me. Those calm sunrise breakfasts with her were the reunion I will actually remember.
CR-131,Elena,Vasquez,married,prefers phone calls,,none,,18,,My grandma tells stories about crossing the border that I am only old enough now to understand. Hearing her tell them again by the fire, with the little ones listening, I finally saw how much of this family she carried here herself.

CR-134,Holden,Price,married,prefers text,,none,,29,,I thought a whole weekend of family togetherness would drive me crazy until my grandfather showed me the little workshop at the cabin. CR-135,Isla,Fernandez,married,prefers voice notes,,none,,5,,I learned three ukulele chords over the winter and finally worked up the nerve to play at the campfire. It was shaky, but the little cousins sang along anyway. Music is easier to share than feelings, and this family sang loudest of all.

Sofia Navarro: Everything still feels temporary, with a new town and a new routine, but sitting around the fire you felt like you belonged to something steady.

Zach Morrison: The quiet cabin porch was where you retreated when the crowd got to be too much. Stepping away and coming back was its own kind of belonging.

Amira Khalil: Money is tight at home, and for one weekend at the lake none of that followed you. You laughed so hard during the three-legged race that you forgot to worry.

Brandon Lee: You tend to keep to yourself at big gatherings. Your cousin handed you a fishing rod and sat with you in silence for an hour.

Chloe Park: You brought two rescue dogs from the shelter, and the family fell in love with a scruffy pit bull named Rusty.

Dante Romano: Big loud group meals are the hardest part, so you ate breakfast early on the quiet porch. Grandma joined you for those sunrise breakfasts.

Elena Vasquez: Your grandma tells stories about crossing the border, and hearing her tell them again by the fire showed how much of this family she carried here.

Finn Murphy: Last fall was rough and you almost skipped the reunion out of pride. Nobody asked why your life looked different. They made space for you at the lake.

Gia Washington: Big group toasts make your chest tight, so you wrote everyone a little note and left them on the pillows.

Holden Price: Your grandfather showed you the little workshop, and you fixed the dock railing together without a single nail.

Isla Fernandez: You learned three ukulele chords over the winter and played at the campfire. It was shaky, and the little cousins sang along.

Jasper Cole: You are not much of a writer, so you dictated most of this walking the lake trail and then cleaned it up. It sounds honest, like the weekend did.

Amina Farouk: The poetry around the fire was your favorite moment. You want to write something for next year's reunion, maybe in Somali.

Nora Lindqvist: You started a journal this fall because Dr. Kaur said it might help. By the reunion you were writing whole paragraphs, and the lake at sunrise made you feel brand new.

Ben Tanaka: You and your son are reading The Hobbit out loud, one chapter every Sunday since the reunion campfire story night. He does the dwarf voices and you do Bilbo.

Tasha Brooks: You used to dread reunions because life feels messy right now, but everyone made room for you. The morning you helped grandma flip pancakes, nobody asked a single hard question.

Derek Foster: Coach Miller said anger is just energy with nowhere to go, so you ran the lake trail every morning. It helped.

Leilani Wong: After your mom's mastectomy you helped with her drains, and bringing her to the lake to see her laugh with her sisters felt like a reward.

Rachel Goldman: Ms. Levin has been teaching you to slow down so your words come out the way you mean them. At the reunion talent night you read a poem out loud, and you are proud.

Sean O'Brien: Mornings are hard because your little brother has autism, so missing the sunrise hike made sense. The afternoon by the lake made up for it.

Tyler Bennett: This reunion was hard, and you have been talking to your mom more. You go to family therapy on Wednesdays now, and writing it down in the memory book is part of trying to do better.

Linh Nguyen: You read on the dock every afternoon and finished three books. Your favorite was A Wrinkle in Time, and you are writing your own story about a girl who can hear what plants are thinking.

Anjali Mehta: You and your little cousin built a reading fort out of blankets and flashlights and read Charlotte's Web together. You cried at the end even though you are the grown-up.

Marcus Reyes: The lake was the only place all weekend where your brain went quiet. You swam out to the raft every afternoon and just floated.

Sofia Navarro: Everything still feels temporary, with a new town and a new routine, but sitting around the fire you felt like you belonged to something steady.

Grandma Chen: Having all of your grandchildren in one kitchen again was the answer to a prayer. You rolled tamales, burned the first batch of pancakes, and nobody minded.

Uma Desai: Cooking with the family reminded you that recipes are instructions you can argue with. You and grandma disagreed about the salt three times and both of you were right.

Victor Chen: People talk fast around the reunion table, but out on the quiet dock at dusk, one conversation at a time, you could finally keep up.

Willa Cross: Scout got sick in January and you almost lost her. Watching her nap in the sun by the lake with the kids was healing.

Xavier Chen: You filmed little clips of the campfire, the cannonball contest, and grandma laughing, and you are cutting them into a short movie.

Yara Aziz: The reunion fell at the end of Ramadan, so you broke your last few fasts at the lake and explained it to the little cousins over dinner.

Zach Morrison: The quiet cabin porch was where you retreated when the crowd got to be too much. Stepping away and coming back was its own kind of belonging.

Amira Khalil: Money is tight at home, and for one weekend at the lake none of that followed you. You laughed so hard during the three-legged race that you forgot to worry.

Brandon Lee: You tend to keep to yourself at big gatherings. Your cousin handed you a fishing rod and sat with you in silence for an hour.

Chloe Park: You brought two rescue dogs from the shelter, and the family fell in love with a scruffy pit bull named Rusty.

Dante Romano: Big loud group meals are the hardest part, so you ate breakfast early on the quiet porch. Grandma joined you for those sunrise breakfasts.

Elena Vasquez: Your grandma tells stories about crossing the border, and hearing her tell them again by the fire showed how much of this family she carried here.

Finn Murphy: Last fall was rough and you almost skipped the reunion out of pride. Nobody asked why your life looked different. They made space for you at the lake.

Gia Washington: Big group toasts make your chest tight, so you wrote everyone a little note and left them on the pillows.

Holden Price: Your grandfather showed you the little workshop, and you fixed the dock railing together without a single nail.

Isla Fernandez: You learned three ukulele chords over the winter and played at the campfire. It was shaky, and the little cousins sang along.

Jasper Cole: You are not much of a writer, so you dictated most of this walking the lake trail and then cleaned it up. It sounds honest, like the weekend did.
